solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shocking no-ball I belted back across stagnant pool

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
across says the answer stretches over the words shocking, no-ball, I and belted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cricketer, angry at a no-ball, whacks the ball back over a muddy pond.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'across' into the definition; it is the hidden-word signal ('across' the words), leaving 'stagnant pool' as the definition. Read backwards inside 'shockinG NO-BALL I Belted'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia a billabong is a cut-off backwater of a river, a still pool left when the water level drops.

clue.text: Orchestral players start to swear, wearing women's underwear

indicators.note: wearing means the second piece is put on inside the garment, so it goes within

parts.note: bras are items of women's underwear

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of swear is used

explanation.surface: Musicians in an orchestra begin cursing while dressed in lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' gives the S of swear, which goes inside BRAS ('wearing').
explanation.definitionFit: The brass section of an orchestra is its trumpets, trombones, horns and tubas, collectively named after the metal.

clue.text: Dropping new name, Lenin no doubt relaxed

indicators.note: dropping says letters are let fall from the name Lenin

parts.note: taken as written: the Russian revolutionary's name
no doubt means surely, certainly

explanation.surface: Lenin, having shed a new name, was presumably at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' takes both Ns from LENIN, leaving LEI, which is followed by SURELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhurried and relaxed are near synonyms: something done at a calm, easy pace.

clue.text: It fights infection in short and underdeveloped bone of the ear

indicators.note: short says the word and loses its final letter
underdeveloped says the bone is not fully grown, so it lacks its last letter

parts.note: the tibia is the shin bone
otic is the adjective meaning relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A medical note about a stunted bone in the ear that fights infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts AND to AN; 'underdeveloped' cuts TIBIA to TIBI. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Penicillin and similar drugs kill or halt bacteria, so a drug of this class is something that combats infection.

clue.text: Provided unlimited coffee and wine

indicators.note: unlimited means without its limits, the first and last letters of coffee

parts.note: red is wine of that colour

explanation.surface: Coffee and wine were supplied without any limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' strips coffee to OFFE.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide something is to put it forward or tender it, a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Dismal delay for airborne migrant

parts.note: a dismal day is grey
a lag is a delay, as in time lag

explanation.surface: A gloomy hold-up for a migrating flier.
explanation.definitionFit: The greylag is a wild goose that flies south in winter, an example of a migratory bird.

clue.text: Acting heads of iffy hedge funds earn trillion nicker

indicators.note: acting suggests a performance, so the letters take on a new role in a different order
heads of means the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Interim bosses of dodgy hedge funds pocketing a trillion pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads of' gives IHFET, rearranged ('Acting'). 'nicker' is British slang for a thief (one who nicks), not the pound it suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to nick is to steal, so a nicker is a stealer.

clue.text: Regularly removing trustful dancer's clothing

indicators.note: regularly removing says every other letter of trustful goes, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A ballerina's costume repeatedly takes away her trust.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping R, S, F, L from trustful leaves the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina wears a short stiff skirt of layered net, the classic ballet costume.

clue.text: Finally getting rid of banks altogether

indicators.note: banks are the edges, so the first and last letters of the word finally are dropped

explanation.surface: At last doing away with banks once and for all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' looks like an indicator for a last letter; it is the word being trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in total, all things considered, the same as altogether.

clue.text: A third of fitted carpeting is non- flammable

indicators.note: a third of means the opening two of the six letters of fitted

parts.note: a carpeting is a telling-off, a reproof

explanation.surface: Part of a fitted carpet is claimed to resist fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpeting' is the British sense of a reprimand (being 'carpeted' by the boss), not floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Material that resists catching fire is non-flammable; the two terms are synonyms.

clue.text: Very famous reporter is half-cut

indicators.note: half-cut says half of the word for reporter is lopped off, its first five letters

parts.note: a reporter is a journalist

explanation.surface: A newsman who is a bit drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for tipsy but here means half the letters are cut away.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-list is the top tier of celebrities, so to be on it is to be very famous.

clue.text: I refer to a play that everyone can watch

indicators.note: play suggests the letters move about freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone directing attention to a theatre show open to all viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' rearranges IREFERTOA.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasts shown without subscription are free-to-air, open to any viewer with a set.

clue.text: Obstinately unshaven guards love sailors

indicators.note: guards means the word for unshaven surrounds the rest

parts.note: an unshaven chin is stubbly
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Bearded men protecting a romance with navy men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' is the container signal, not security staff; 'love' is the tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting obstinately is acting in a pig-headed, unyielding way.

clue.text: Applaud evacuation of central Antwerp

indicators.note: evacuation empties the words central and Antwerp, leaving just their outside letters

explanation.surface: Cheering the clearing of people from downtown Antwerp.
explanation.definitionFit: To clap is to strike the hands together in approval, a synonym of applaud.

clue.text: Unimaginative lot fated to wander around Foreign Office

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters sit on either side of the next piece
wander says the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A dull bunch are doomed to drift around the diplomatic service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wander' scrambles 'lot fated', and the jumble sits 'around' the Foreign Office abbreviation, splitting four letters before and four after.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat-footed figuratively means clumsy and lacking imagination or quick wit.

clue.text: Tiny step in the direction of European dominance

parts.note: to means towards, in the direction of
a hold over someone is power or dominance

explanation.surface: A small move towards European supremacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A toehold is a small foothold, a slight first step to establishing a position.

clue.text: Leaves boxes of pine to be engulfed by matches

indicators.note: to be engulfed by says the word for pine goes inside the word for matches

parts.note: test matches are the big cricket internationals, so matches are tests
to pine is to ache, yearn

explanation.surface: Someone abandons crates made of pine wood among matchsticks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' is a noun (tea leaves), and 'pine' the verb to yearn, not the timber. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea chests are large wooden crates in which tea leaves were shipped.

clue.text: He observed heavenly bodies of female stars on island

indicators.note: on says the stars are placed next to the island, following it

parts.note: a gal is a girl, a female
Leo is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: A man who looked at the shapes of women celebrities on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavenly bodies' suggests attractive figures; 'stars' is the constellation LEO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian astronomer pointed his telescope at Jupiter's moons and the planets.

clue.text: Unfinished business observed by policeman behind WC

indicators.note: behind says the following pieces come after the word for WC

parts.note: loo is British informal for a toilet, a WC
observed means seen
DS is a Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: A policeman spotted lurking behind a lavatory with business to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose ends are details still to be tied up, things not yet settled.

clue.text: Use amenity whenever you like

indicators.note: use suggests the word is employed or reworked, here into a new order of letters

explanation.surface: A sign inviting people to use a facility at their convenience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use' rearranges AMENITY.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at any hour or moment you choose, exactly whenever you like.

clue.text: Repetitive strain injury of Mr A Rowe

indicators.note: injury suggests the name of the man is damaged and so jumbled

explanation.surface: A man named Rowe suffers from RSI.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' is a tune, not muscle stress, and 'injury of' rearranges MRAROWE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune that loops endlessly in your head is a catchy refrain, repeated in the mind.

clue.text: Extremely saturnine posh chap devours seconds and explodes

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, first and last, of saturnine
devours means the word for posh chap swallows the next piece

parts.note: a toff is a British upper-class man

explanation.surface: A gloomy aristocrat wolfs down second helpings and then erupts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes only the ends of saturnine; 'devours' puts seconds inside the posh chap, a toff being British slang for an upper-class man.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to detonate it; intransitively a thing goes off or explodes.

clue.text: Watch predecessor put students up

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: put down means laid
NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: An earlier guard who put up the students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LAIDNUS end to end. 'Watch' means a timepiece, not a sentry.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadow clocks told the time long before mechanical timepieces were invented.

clue.text: Initially hoping beer is healthy

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of hoping

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A hopeful drinker claims beer is good for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Hale, as in hale and hearty, means strong and in good health.

clue.text: Grub of spectacular variety

indicators.note: of says the answer is made out of letters of the words spectacular variety

explanation.surface: Food from a showy range of dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like food; it is the insect sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect grub is the young wingless stage, the immature form of a beetle.

clue.text: He drugs old ladies, a niche interest

parts.note: gran is a grandmother, an old lady; a gran-doper drugs them generally
a doper is one who drugs

explanation.surface: A sinister man who sedates elderly women, and a minority pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'He drugs old ladies' as GRAN DOPER: one who dopes grans.
explanation.definitionFit: Large-scale serious opera, sung throughout, attracts a devoted but small audience.

clue.text: Collect idiot's confession

definitions.meaning: to collect is to gather together a quantity
a fool admitting what he is would say I am a donkey, split as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as AM ASS, what an idiot would own up to.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect and to gather together a store of something are synonyms.

clue.text: Self-satisfied fools moving closer to summit

indicators.note: the closer is the last letter, moved to the top of this down entry

parts.note: mugs are dupes, fools

explanation.surface: Complacent idiots climbing towards a mountain top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closer' is the final letter, not 'nearer'; it moves from the bottom of MUGS to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes someone excessively pleased with themselves, complacent.

clue.text: Italian smoker from Bristol prancing round home unclothed

indicators.note: round means the scrambled letters surround the next piece
prancing suggests the letters cavort into a new order
unclothed means home is stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: A cigarette-puffing Italian from Bristol dancing about his house naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prancing' scrambles Bristol and 'round' wraps it about home 'unclothed'. 'smoker' is not a person but a volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Stromboli is an active volcano off Sicily, constantly smoking.

clue.text: Georgia Brown swapped briefs

definitions.note: a tanga is one pair of briefs, so plural in form

indicators.note: swapped says the two pieces exchange places from the order in the clue

parts.note: tan is a light brown
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A woman named Georgia Brown exchanged her underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgia Brown' looks like a name; 'swapped' says its two parts change places.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanga is a skimpy style of underwear, minimal briefs joined at the hips by thin strips.

clue.text: Liberal dons tweeted in the vernacular

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the word for tweeted wears the next letter inside

parts.note: birds tweet, that is, sang

explanation.surface: Liberal-minded academics posted online in plain everyday language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' are not academics but 'puts on': SANG takes in L. 'tweeted' is birdsong, not social media.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal everyday speech, the vernacular rather than formal language.

clue.text: Films about Berlioz oddly ignored last of old tunesmiths

indicators.note: about means the word for films goes round the rest

parts.note: a film is a thin haze, a mist

indicators.note: oddly ignored says the odd-placed letters of Berlioz are dropped, keeping the even ones
last of means the final letter of old

explanation.surface: Movies about the composer Berlioz neglect the final old tunesmiths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly ignored' keeps the even letters of Berlioz; 'about' puts them, with the last of old, inside the films word. Films here are hazes, not movies.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodists are composers of melodies, writers of tunes.
